did_you_know.text: Did you know? The LORD commanded Jeremiah to write on a scroll everything that had been spoken to him from the days of Josiah until that time, including prophecies about Israel, Judah, and the nations.

Did you know? The purpose of writing the scroll was not merely to record the prophecies: the people were urged to hear the warnings, turn from their evil ways, and thereby receive forgiveness for their sins and offenses.
Did you know? Jeremiah did not write the scroll himself. Instead, he dictated the words of the LORD to Baruch son of Neriah, and Baruch wrote them on a scroll.
Did you know? Jeremiah explained that he was confined and therefore could not go to the house of the LORD. Instead, he sent Baruch to read the scroll to the people on a day of fasting.

Did you know? The scroll was read to the people in the fifth year of Jehoiakim, in the ninth month, during a fast proclaimed in Jerusalem that was attended by people who had also come from the towns of Judah.

Did you know? Baruch read the scroll in the chamber of Gemariah son of Shaphan, in the upper courtyard of the house of the LORD, near the entrance of the New Gate of the LORD’s house, in the hearing of all the people.
Did you know? When the officials asked Baruch how he had written the words, he replied that Jeremiah had dictated them to him, and he had written them in the scroll with ink.

Did you know? King Jehoiakim did more than simply ignore the scroll: whenever Jehudi had read three or four sections, the king cut them off with a scribe’s knife and threw them into the fire until the entire scroll was burned.
Did you know? After the king ordered Jeremiah and Baruch to be arrested, they could not be found because the LORD had hidden them, as the passage explains.
Did you know? The scroll that was rewritten contained everything that had been in the first scroll, but the passage adds that many more words of prophecy were also included.
